item.title: A Full Post
item.dc:creator: Fixture Writer
item.content:encoded:
This is the full body of the post, carried entirely inside the feed. It is comfortably long enough that the importer should not attempt to fetch the canonical page at all, because the feed content is already substantial and complete. Paragraph one makes an argument.

Paragraph two develops the argument further with several more sentences of filler prose so that the total length of this content easily clears the two thousand character threshold used by the importer to decide whether a feed item is a mere excerpt or the real article body.

Paragraph three continues at some length, because the threshold in question is deliberately generous: many feeds carry summaries of six or seven hundred characters that look substantial but are actually truncations of much longer essays, and the importer needs to be suspicious of anything that could plausibly be a summary rather than a complete piece of writing. So this fixture keeps talking, sentence after sentence, in the manner of a writer who has discovered that word count is occasionally a feature rather than a vice, until the accumulated prose safely exceeds the level at which the importer would consider reaching out to the canonical page for a fuller version of the text.

Paragraph four exists purely as ballast. It restates the premise of the previous paragraphs with minor variations, notes that restating premises with minor variations is a time-honored technique for reaching a required length, observes that the technique is being deployed at this very moment, and then observes the observation itself, recursively, until the character counter on the authoring side of this fixture finally ticks past the two thousand mark and the paragraph is permitted, at long last, to end.

Paragraph five concludes the argument with a flourish and a final sentence long enough to remove any lingering doubt about the total character count, which by this point has climbed well clear of the threshold and continues climbing anyway, out of an abundance of caution and a mild commitment to the bit.
